taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a shrub 1 m to 4 m tall.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: shrub or small tree, 1-6 m. high; FEIS: 2 to 20 feet (0.5 to 6 m).

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Rhus glabra: a native, perennial, deciduous, thicket-forming shrub or small tree.

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Rhus glabra: a shrub or small tree; branches sparse, smooth and stout.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Rhus glabra: deciduous.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Leaves borne singly, alternate along the stems, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 86660193, 172071490, 163892106, 26818318, 25522053, 51724636, 137135792, 222347559): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets 11-31.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets 11-31, pinnately arranged with a terminal one, as in the photos.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets serrulate, not divided again.

traits.leaflets.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets 11-31.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: An odd leaflet at each leaf's tip, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 86660193, 172071490, 163892106, 26818318, 25522053, 51724636, 137135792, 222347559): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves 30 cm to 50 cm long.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 2.5-10 cm. long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 12 cm to 25 cm across their leaflets, as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 4 cm to 10 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: leaflets acuminate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: sharply serrulate.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: inflorescence a large dense terminal panicle.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Upright panicles at the shoot tips, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 86660193, 172071490, 163892106, 26818318, 25522053, 51724636, 137135792, 222347559): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Rhus glabra: flowers borne in long (up to 18 inches (45 cm)), dense, compound, terminal panicles; 10 cm to 25 cm usual (species-facts estimate).

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: 12 to 25 side branches to a panicle, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 86660193, 172071490, 163892106, 26818318, 25522053, 51724636, 137135792, 222347559): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: several hundred to a thousand small flowers in a panicle, as in the photos.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: flowers greenish, about 3 mm. broad.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: flowers greenish; drawn yellow-green as in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.sexual_system.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: dioecious.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: drupe compressed.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: drupe about 4 mm. in diameter.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: drupe covered with short reddish hairs; the photos show dark red clusters; sRGB by eye.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus glabra: flowering May to July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: drupes ripe August to October.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a sparsely branched, open shrub of long feathery leaves of many narrow leaflets, crowned with upright yellow-green panicles that turn to dark red fruit.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for smooth sumac from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 2.6 m tall at 12 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, phase C batch 3 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from Abrams, FEIS and Dendrology, counts from photos.
